narrationTexts: I'll start by finding the remaining `db.query` call sites.
Vendor file is explicitly "do not edit" (replaced on upgrade), so I'll leave it and flag it. Reading the 12 first-party files.
Now verifying and checking for tests.
finalText:
Migration done. 12 first-party files, 36 call sites converted from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `src/repo/session.js`, `src/service/teamService.js`, `src/admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `src/repo/refund.js`, `src/service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `src/repo/supplier.js`, `src/admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `src/repo/shipment.js`, `src/service/returnService.js` |
| support | `src/repo/sla.js`, `src/admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `src/repo/cohort.js` |

Each file had the same three shapes (get-by-id, list, update); I matched the wording and formatting of the already-migrated files like `packages/billing/src/repo/subscription.js`. All 12 pass `node --check`. There are no tests or package.json in the repo, so that's the extent of the verification I could do.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** — the only remaining `db.query` calls. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local edits silently lost. Migrating it would be reverted by the next upgrade, so it needs either an upstream fix or a shim on your side. Worth deciding before the driver's next major drops `query`, since `lib/db.js` says it will.
- **`cache.query(...)`** in the various `cached*` helpers — that's `lib/cache.js`, a different API, not part of this migration.
